reader.requirement: At 1985 an ADD, COMPUTE, DIVIDE, MULTIPLY or SUBTRACT with several resultants evaluates its initial operands once into a temporary and then stores that value into (or combines it with) each resultant in the written left-to-right order, each resultant identified, with its subscripts, only when its own store is reached, so a subscript reads the value an earlier resultant of the same statement stored.

edition-consulted.switches: DialectBehavior.UnphrasedSizeErrorIsFatal: below 2002 a statement without ON SIZE ERROR catches every condition and goes on to the next resultant and the next statement; from 2002 the condition is fatal
only the citation text (Edition.Cite) of format diagnostics
refuses the 2014 ROUNDED MODE IS phrase on a resultant at 1985 (COBOL0803)

reader.edition-search: grep of Edition.|CobolVersion|IsAtLeast|DialectBehavior in ArithmeticEmitter.cs, ReceiverBracketEmitter.cs, SendingValueTemp.cs and ArithmeticBinder.cs; the order of stores and identification at store is one arm
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: yes: only the unphrased size error, which at 1985 leaves the affected resultant undefined and continues (§1985:VI.6.4.2 GR3) and at 2023 ends the run unit for a zero divisor; the multiple-result sequence itself is the same
reader.witnesses-cover: part: the witnesses cover ADD/SUBTRACT/MULTIPLY receivers and identification at store; DIVIDE INTO and GIVING forms, COMPUTE with a subscripted later receiver, relative subscripts, packed and binary subscripts, two-level subscripts and the per-resultant size error are not exercised

reader.notes: Every verb's multiple-result form reproduces the GR2 equivalences, including subscripts that read an earlier resultant's new value (ReceiverBracketEmitter runs each receiver's identification at its own store). Probe class a and e do not apply to this rule. DISPLAY shows an unedited 9V9 as 1.5, which is the implementor's conversion under §1985:VI.6.10.4 GR1 and is outside this rule.
reader.at-2023: mres1 semantics are one arm; mres6 at 2023 ends with EC-SIZE-ZERO-DIVIDE as 2002+ requires

refuter.evidence: Probes aimed at a resultant that is also an initial-evaluation operand, which the reader's probes touched only through subscripts. rmr1 at --std 85 (runs/rmr1-001), the same at 2023 (rmr1-002): ADD A TO A, B gives A=+002 B=+011 (the temp is the original A); ADD A B TO B, C gives B=+023 C=+113; SUBTRACT A FROM A, B gives A=+000 B=+006; MULTIPLY A BY A, B gives A=+009 B=+030; DIVIDE A INTO A, B gives A=+001 B=+020; ADD A B GIVING A, C and MULTIPLY A BY B GIVING A, C store one temp into both (5,5 and 6,6); COMPUTE X, Y = X + 1 gives X=Y=+008; DIVIDE A BY B GIVING A, C gives 5,5; ADD 1 TO A, A applies twice (A=+007); ADD 50 TO P, P ON SIZE ERROR stores 60, then the second store overflows and P keeps 60 with SE shown; COMPUTE I, T (I) = T (I) + 1 reads T(2) initially and stores into T(6); ADD T (I) TO I, T (I) stores 4 into T(7); SUBTRACT T (I) FROM 9 GIVING I, T (I) ROUNDED stores 9 into T(9). Each matches the per-verb initial evaluation rules (VI.6.6.4 GR1/GR2, VI.6.26.4 GR1/GR2, VI.6.20.4 GR1, VI.6.11.4 GR1/GR2) and the GR2 sequence. rmrr1: the 2002 COMPUTE ... EQUAL form is refused at 85 (COBOL0001 near EQUAL; the 1985 format prints only =). Edition sites: ArithmeticEmitter.cs#EmitArith (DialectBehavior.UnphrasedSizeErrorIsFatal) is the only behavioural switch, already in the reader's list; ArithmeticBinder.cs consults the edition only for citation text. cite.py: OK §1985:VI.6.4.6 GR2; OK §1985:VI.6.4.6 GR1.
